item.title: Go Daily Question 20250529
item.description:
What is the output of the following code?

package main

import "fmt"

type Math struct {
	x, y int
}

var m = map[string]Math{
	"foo": Math{2, 3},
}

func main() {
	m["foo"].x = 4
	fmt.Println(m["foo"].x)
}

A. 4 B. compilation error

🔑 Answer Analysis:

Reference answer and explanation: B, compilation error cannot assign to struct field m["foo"].x in map. Reason for error: For an assignment operation similar to X = Y, the address of X must be known to assign the value of Y to X, but the value of a map itself in Go is not addressable.

item.title: Go Daily Question 094
item.description:
What is the output of the following code?

type Math struct {
    x, y int
}

var m = map[string]Math{
    "foo": Math{2, 3},
}

func main() {
    m["foo"].x = 4
    fmt.Println(m["foo"].x)
}

A. 4 B. compilation error

🔑 Answer Analysis:

Reference answer and explanation: B, compilation error “cannot assign to struct field m[“foo”].x in map”. The reason for the error is that for an assignment operation like X = Y, the address of X must be known to assign the value of Y to X. However, in Go, the value of a map itself is not addressable.

item.title: Go Daily Question 026
item.description:
Will the following code compile?

package main

import "fmt"

type Student struct {
    Name string
}

var list map[string]Student

func main() {

    list = make(map[string]Student)

    student := Student{"Aceld"}

    list["student"] = student
    list["student"].Name = "LDB"

    fmt.Println(list["student"])
}
🔑 Answer Analysis:

Answer: Compilation fails. The value of map[string]Student is a Student struct value, so when list["student"] = student, it’s a value copy process. However, list["student"] then becomes a value reference. The characteristic of a value reference is that it is read-only. Therefore, modifying list["student"].Name = "LDB" is not allowed.
